newsitem.title: USA: Fonar says high court tells GE to pay $103m.
newsitem.headline: Fonar says high court tells GE to pay $103m.

text.p: Fonar Corp on Wednesday said the U.S. Supreme Court has refused to block a $103 million patent infringement penalty against General Electric Co while GE appeals the fine to the high court.
The ruling was issued without comment by Chief Justice William Rehnquist, the company said.

In 1995, a federal jury awarded Fonar $103 million in connection with its complaint that GE had infringed on two of Fonar's magnetic resonance imaging patents, the company said. GE appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals, which upheld the District Court award.

GE asked the Supreme Court for a stay of the penalty while it awaited word of its petition to have the high court review the lower court rulings. The Supreme Court has not decided whether it will take the case.
The patents that District Court jurors determined were violated by GE were the "Cancer Detection Patent" -- the world's first MRI patent -- and the "Mutli-angle Oblique Patent," the company said.
